note: Seed item. The gradient runs through the headline and the waveform as well as the background, which is what stops the glass reading as a sticker. Replace this note with your own.

typography.headingCharacter: Humanist grotesque at display size with tight leading, where a whole clause carries a violet to cyan to rose gradient as its fill while the surrounding lines stay solid white.
typography.bodyCharacter: Same family at reading size in a muted lavender rather than full white, generous leading, with small tracked labels inside the glass panel.

composition.structure: A floating pill navigation detached from the top edge, a left headline and body column, and a large translucent player card overlapping thin orbit rings that bleed off the right edge, with three feature cards along the foot.

spacing.rhythm: Long vertical rests between the badge, headline, body and buttons, with dense evenly spaced rows inside the player card so the panel feels like an instrument set into open space.

surfaceTreatment.finish: Frosted translucent panels over a soft gradient mesh, each edged with a one pixel light-catching border and lifted on a wide soft shadow. The nav and the primary button are full pills; the panels are large radius rectangles.

imagery.treatment: No photography. A gradient mesh background carrying violet, teal and rose blooms, combined with a rendered interface panel and thin concentric orbit rings used as abstract structure.

philosophy.text: The design treats depth as the whole medium. Nothing sits flat on the background because the background is not a colour but a field of light, and every surface is a pane held some distance in front of it. The gradient is the unifying device rather than an effect applied once: it runs through the mesh, through one clause of the headline and through the waveform, so the page reads as a single continuous light source rather than a dark theme with accents dropped on top. Restraint shows up in the type, which stays plain and humanist while everything around it glows, and that contrast is what keeps the result feeling engineered rather than decorative.
